name: Chart
description: Encoding-driven chart. One component for the whole family: choose a mark and map data fields to visual channels.

generation.purpose: Show how a measure varies across a dimension, optionally split into series.
generation.whenToUse: Whenever the data has a dimension — a trend over time, a breakdown by category, a comparison across series. Choose the mark from the question: 'bar' for counts by category, 'line' or 'area' for a trend over time, 'point' for scatter. Use stacking 'stacked' when the parts sum to a meaningful whole.
generation.whenNotToUse: Do not use for a single aggregated figure — use analytics.kpi-card. Do not use for record-level detail — use data.table.

stacking.description: Only meaningful when a series encoding is bound.

segmentActivated.label: Segment activated
segmentActivated.description: Emitted when a bar or point is clicked or activated with Enter. Typically mapped to a setFilter action so clicking a segment filters the rest of the page.

series.description: Series key, or null when no series encoding is bound.

retryRequested.label: Retry requested
retryRequested.description: Emitted when the user activates Retry in the error state.

xs.note: Axis labels thin out automatically as width decreases.

accessibility.keyboardContract: Bars and points are focusable buttons with an accessible label naming the series, category and value. Enter activates.
accessibility.notes: A figcaption contains a data-table equivalent of every plotted value, so the chart is fully readable without seeing it. Series are distinguishable by legend text, not colour alone.

lifecycle.migrationNote: M1 implements the bar, line, area and point marks with linear and band scales. Log and time scales, y2 and the size/shape channels are declared in the schema but not yet rendered.
